title: ChargeWise Fits the Fleet to the Grid
summary: Building ChargeWise AI with physical charging constraints, independent schedule checks, an editable browser demo, Nemotron tools, and a forecasting follow-up.
whyItMatters: A feasible charging schedule can reveal how much grid capacity a depot actually needs before more hardware or a larger connection is considered.
feedDescription: An editable browser charging demo, four-van capacity proof, tariff trade-offs, outage replanning, and a 26 October forecasting follow-up.

title: When Do AI Outputs Tip?
summary: Sixteen attention-head interventions, a mathematical response clock, and cache edits that hold current answers fixed. Research notes on the state a language model carries between answers.
whyItMatters: The probability of a correct answer may omit information needed to predict later errors or choose when to intervene.
feedDescription: Measured head-content versus routing interventions, an interactive mathematical error clock, and ongoing experiments on matched present readouts with different internal states.

title: Gold Medals Don't Stack Batteries: Building Training Grounds for AI Agents
summary: From programming medals to battery stacking: verifiable environments, six 2026 agent and robotics projects, and practical tests for learning rewards, recovery, and resets.
whyItMatters: An agent can improve only if its practice environment rewards the work we actually need done. Reliable feedback is what connects impressive answers to useful actions.
feedDescription: From RL textbooks and VERA to RoboReward, FLARE, REVOLVE, Isaac GR00T, and RoboDojo: how 2026 projects train rewards, recovery, and resets, with reported results and a proposed electrode-handling test design.

title: Price Wars: East vs. West Battery Production and the SynBatt Response
summary: One animated timeline of manufacturers and factory plans. Grouped company cases connect funding, ramp-up, and customer demand, alongside twenty price-gap mechanisms and the SynBatt response.
whyItMatters: Cheaper, reliable battery production helps clean energy scale. Knowing which costs engineering can change makes the next investment more useful.
feedDescription: A sourced timeline of EV battery deployment and factory milestones, twenty reasons regional battery prices differ, six 2026 publications, and the SynBatt projects addressing manufacturing costs.

title: How to (Not) Reinvent the Wheel With Jeff
summary: Jev, Jeff, and typed decisions: shared representations, task-specific heads, calibrated probabilities, and a concrete policy for when a manufacturing model acts or requests review.
whyItMatters: Turning a model’s output into a clear decision makes it easier to use and check in a manufacturing workflow.
feedDescription: Jev, Jeff, and typed decisions: shared representations, task-specific heads, calibrated probabilities, and a concrete policy for when a manufacturing model acts or requests review.

title: DisCo and the Case for Reusable Agent Skills
summary: DisCo distills repositories and papers into reusable operating skills. Scope, ground, construct, and verify: a practical route from research knowledge to repeatable workflows.
whyItMatters: Reusable, checked procedures can help research agents build on existing work rather than repeat setup and mistakes.
feedDescription: DisCo distills repositories and papers into reusable operating skills. Scope, ground, construct, and verify: a practical route from research knowledge to repeatable workflows.

title: Reading ConvMem: Long-Context Reasoning as a Summary Tree
summary: ConvMem reads a long document as a tree of question-conditioned summaries instead of a chain of memory updates, which cuts the path from a fact to the answer from linear to logarithmic. Notes on the method, results and cost, and seven ideas for a path shorter than logarithmic.
whyItMatters: How a system condenses a long document determines whether the facts needed for an answer survive.
feedDescription: Reading notes on ConvMem (arXiv:2609.10441): hierarchical summarization with overlapping windows, skip connections and sub-question channels, compared with MemAgent, plus ideas for constant-depth long-context reasoning.

title: I Checked 2,294 arXiv Equations for Upside-Down Fractions
summary: Copying rendered math from a chat window can put a fraction's denominator first. I reviewed every display equation in 60 arXiv papers and pattern-checked 200: 4.9% of display equations have a meaning-changing error, 2 of 118 errors are inverted fractions, and the rate did not change between 2021 and 2026.
whyItMatters: A copied equation can change meaning without looking wrong, so reliable scientific workflows need checks beyond fluent text.
feedDescription: How often are equations in arXiv papers wrong, how many of the errors are inverted fractions, and did that change after 2022? A review of 2,294 display equations in 60 papers plus pattern checks on 200.

title: I Ran a Game-Theory RL-Menu Agent in GLEE for 48 Hours (No LLM)
summary: A weekend building a no-LLM game-theory bot for the GLEE economic games (bargaining, negotiation, persuasion), and what actually moved the percentile score: scaling the reward, measuring in the right seat, and closing before inflation eats the pot. Includes a playable version of the three games.
whyItMatters: An agent that wins in simulation can still lose against real opponents, making evaluation design as important as the strategy.
feedDescription: Notes from building a game-theory agent for GLEE: what moved the percentile score (reward scaling, same-seat baseline, closing before inflation) and what did not (persuasive messages, hard anchoring). With a playable version of the three games.

title: Finding a Fair Evaluation Under Changing Representations
summary: Certified retention is easy for frozen features and collapses once the representation moves. A bottom-up stripe benchmark that makes adaptation provably necessary, and CARG, the metric for the accuracy you lose when the retention certificate has to hold.
whyItMatters: A learning system should be tested on whether it can adapt and remember when its internal representation changes.
feedDescription: Certified retention under a changing representation: a bottom-up stripe benchmark where a frozen encoder provably cannot win, and the CARG metric for the accuracy-retention tradeoff.

title: The Student Becomes the Teacher
summary: Three 2026 papers let a language model supply its own supervision, the external teacher, the ground-truth labels, and the privileged context, all replaced by the model itself. What it buys, and where it breaks.
whyItMatters: Models that teach themselves could reduce the need for labelled data, but they can also reinforce their own mistakes.
feedDescription: On-policy self-distillation without labels: OPSD, U-OPSD's label-free majority vote, and L-OPSD's learnable privileged context, with the failure modes that come with self-supervision.

title: From Simulating Speech to Optimizing Reasoning
summary: Three 2026 papers argue chain-of-thought text was never the reasoning. Reasoning is a latent direction, activated early, held in superposition, and compressible to a few tokens.
whyItMatters: Understanding what drives a model’s reasoning helps judge whether a convincing explanation reflects how it reached an answer.
feedDescription: Reading notes: 2026 evidence that LLM reasoning is a latent computational mode only loosely coupled to the chain-of-thought text printed alongside it.

title: The Race to O(n)
summary: Every subquadratic-attention family relaxes one constraint while quietly keeping another. Five families, the routing-absorption trap, and why the frontier keeps flinching back to dense attention.
whyItMatters: Making AI cheaper to run requires understanding what faster attention methods trade away.
feedDescription: Reading notes across the subquadratic-attention literature: pruning, learned selection, linear memory, delta-rule correction, and the impossibility proofs.

title: Lithium Dendrites Are Batteries' Dandelions
summary: Ceramic solid electrolytes still fail by dendrite. A March 2026 model derives a closed-form critical current density from first principles, and writes down the same physics that lets a dandelion crack a driveway.
whyItMatters: Understanding how tiny defects grow into battery short circuits can help guide safer material and process choices.
feedDescription: A first-principles model of critical current density for alkali-metal dendrites in ceramic solid electrolytes, read through the physics of a dandelion cracking pavement.

title: AI's Bottleneck Is Physical
summary: AI becomes truly useful when a physical feedback loop (power, heat, latency, sensors, data lineage, safe actuation) can run reliably. Where the loop is closed and why capability is not deployability.
whyItMatters: AI can support real experiments and production only when sensing, computation, and physical action work reliably together.
feedDescription: The next bottleneck in AI is physical: whether the loop from electricity through inference to actuation and back to sensors can run reliably, efficiently, and observably.

title: Reading CausalPFN: Causal Effects as In-Context Prediction
summary: A NeurIPS 2025 paper trains one transformer on simulated, identifiable causal worlds; new observational data goes in as context, treatment-effect posteriors come out. What holds it up, and where it breaks.
whyItMatters: Distinguishing causes from correlations is essential when a model is used to choose what to change in a process.
feedDescription: Notes on Balazadeh et al., CausalPFN: one transformer, trained on simulated identifiable DGPs, that estimates treatment effects in-context.

title: The Geometry of Forgetting in Continual Learning
summary: How learning a new task damages an old one, and how interference geometry suggests a structural controller.
whyItMatters: Models that keep learning need a way to preserve useful earlier knowledge while adapting to new data.
feedDescription: Forgetting as interference energy under a task's feature covariance, and the IGFA controller.

title: Solving the Electrode Calendering U-Shape Puzzle
summary: Why particle reorientation reverses the monotone prediction made by porosity-only thermal models.
whyItMatters: Connecting electrode processing to heat transport helps explain why pressing an electrode harder does not always improve its thermal behaviour.
feedDescription: Why through-plane conductivity dips before it rises, and the closure that captures it.
